### What's new
- **Preview HTML files.** **View › Show Preview** (**⇧⌘V**) and the title bar toggle now work for .html, .htm and .xhtml files as they do for Markdown. The page is shown as a browser would show it, with its styles, images and scripts, and with your unsaved changes. Web links open in your browser and links to project files open in a Silica tab. - **Preview CSV and TSV files as a table.** The same toggle shows a .csv or .tsv file as a table with a header row that stays at the top and numeric columns aligned right. Double-click a row to go to its line in the source. Very large files are cut off at 100,000 cells, with a note saying how many rows there are. - **PDFs open in the editor.** A PDF file now opens in its own tab instead of showing as a binary file. A password-protected PDF asks for its password. - **Video files play in the editor.** Videos open in a player, with the picture's size, length and file size beneath it. Each tab keeps its place in its video, and a video pauses when you switch away from its tab. - **Animated GIFs play in the image viewer.** A GIF, animated PNG or animated WebP now plays in its tab, where only its first frame was shown. - **Diff and patch files are highlighted.** .diff, .patch and .rej files, and diff code blocks in the Markdown preview, show added lines in green and removed lines in red in every theme. - **Drag files and folders out of the sidebar.** Drag a row from the file tree to another app as you would from Finder: Terminal inserts its path, and Finder or the Desktop gets a copy. The file is never moved. - **Drag the project folder from its name.** Hovering the project name at the top of the sidebar shows the folder's Finder icon. Drag it to Terminal to insert the project's path, or to Finder to copy the folder. - **Reveal a tab's file in the explorer.** Right-click a tab and choose **Reveal in Explorer** to open the folders above the file and select it in the file tree. - **Close a tab with a middle click.** - **Set the sidebar's font size.** **Settings › Fonts & Colors** has a new **Sidebar** group with a size from 9 to 20 pt, separate from the editor font. The file tree and the Find in Project results follow it. - **Folders show their Finder icons in the file tree.** Custom folder icons appear, and packages such as .xcodeproj look like what they are. - **Sidebar buttons highlight under the pointer.** The Collapse Folders, Search and sidebar toggle buttons now show a soft fill on hover, like toolbar buttons in system apps. - **Large Markdown previews no longer hold up the window.** The preview is now prepared in the background.
If you already have Silica, it will offer this update on its own, or choose **Silica › Check for Updates…**.
Found a bug or have an idea? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).

### What's new
- **Parent folders stay in view in the file tree.** Scrolled deep into a project, the open folders that contain the rows you're looking at now stay pinned at the top of the tree. Click a pinned folder to scroll back to it. It's on by default; turn it off in **Settings › General**. - **Switch tabs from the keyboard.** **⌃Tab** and **⌃⇧Tab** (or **⇧⌘]** and **⇧⌘[**) step through the open tabs, going round from either end to the other. The commands are also in the **View** menu as Select Next Tab and Select Previous Tab. - **Scroll the tab bar with a mouse wheel.** With the pointer over the tab bar, an ordinary mouse wheel now scrolls the tabs sideways, so tabs past the end of the bar can be reached without a trackpad. - **The tab bar keeps the active tab in view.** Resizing the window or the sidebar no longer scrolls the tab row back to its first tab. - **Tabs fade out at the ends of the tab bar.** A tab scrolled part of the way out now fades instead of being cut off flat. - **The minimap is hidden by default.** Turn it back on with **View › Minimap** or in **Settings › Editor**.
If you already have Silica, it will offer this update on its own, or choose **Silica › Check for Updates…**.
Found a bug or have an idea? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).

### What's new
- **Drag tabs to reorder them.** Drag an editor tab along the tab bar and the tabs it passes slide aside. With more tabs than fit, holding it near either end scrolls the bar. - **A steadier selection in the file tree.** The selected file or folder is now always highlighted in grey. It used to turn blue at times, such as after renaming a file.
If you already have Silica, it will offer this update on its own, or choose **Silica › Check for Updates…**.
Found a bug or have an idea? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).

### What's new
- **Runs on macOS 26.** Silica now needs macOS 26 or later, down from macOS 27. - **A nicer installer.** The DMG opens to a window with Silica and your Applications folder side by side, so installing is one drag.
If you already have 0.1.0, Silica will offer this update on its own, or choose **Silica › Check for Updates…**.
Found a bug or have an idea? Please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).

The first release of Silica, a lightweight code editor for macOS, made of glass.
### What's in it
- **Projects.** Open a folder to get a window with a file tree that follows changes on disk and dims what your `.gitignore` excludes. Create, rename and trash files right in the tree, and filter it as you type. - **Quick Open (⌘P)** with fuzzy matching, and **Find in Project (⇧⌘F)**. - **Syntax highlighting** for 25 languages, including Swift, JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust, C, C++ and Markdown. - **Nine color themes**, each with a light and a dark palette: Atom One, GitHub, Xcode, Solarized, Catppuccin, Gruvbox, Tokyo Night, Rosé Pine and Dracula. - **Markdown preview (⇧⌘V)**, with highlighted code blocks. - **Editing tools**: tabs, line numbers, indent guides, a minimap, word wrap, Go to Line (⌘L), toggle comment (⌘/), and moving or duplicating lines (⌥↑ ⌥↓). - Projects **reopen their tabs** where you left them, and recent projects are on the welcome window. - **Open With** in Finder, the Dock icon and `open -a Silica` all open files and folders in Silica.
### Installing
Open the DMG and drag Silica to Applications. Silica needs macOS 27 or later.
From now on, Silica checks for updates once a day and installs them for you. You can also use **Silica › Check for Updates…**, or turn automatic checks off in Settings › General.
### Feedback
This is an early release, so expect some rough edges. If you find a bug or have an idea, please [open an issue](https://github.com/dqhieu/Silica/issues).
